title: Fatima Sana Returns to Lead Pakistan Women's Cricket Squad for Asia Cup and Asian Games
excerpt: The 22-year-old fast bowler, who left the T20 World Cup after her father's sudden death, is back as captain as Pakistan announce squads for two major tournaments with Wahab Riaz retained as coach.
body:
• Fatima Sana returns as Pakistan women's captain for the ACC Women's Asia Cup and Asian Games after leaving the T20 World Cup following her father's death.
  • The 22-year-old became the youngest player to captain Pakistan at a T20 World Cup, delivering a Player of the Match performance against Sri Lanka before her departure.
  • Former fast bowler Wahab Riaz has been retained as head coach for both tournaments, continuing the rebuild that began after Pakistan's last-place finish at the 2025 ODI World Cup.
  • Pakistan's Asia Cup campaign will feature a high-profile clash against India, adding another chapter to South Asian cricket's fiercest women's rivalry.

Fatima Sana has been named captain of Pakistan's women's cricket squads for the upcoming ACC Women's Asia Cup and Asian Games, according to announcements from the Pakistan Cricket Board. Her return marks one of the more compelling personal comebacks in women's cricket this year.

A Captain's Painful Exit

Sana, a right-arm fast bowler and hard-hitting lower-order batter, was leading Pakistan at the ICC Women's T20 World Cup when her father died suddenly from a stroke. She flew home to Karachi mid-tournament, leaving vice-captain Muneeba Ali to take over leadership duties.

Her departure was a significant blow. In just her first T20 World Cup match as captain, Sana had delivered a Player of the Match performance against Sri Lanka — top-scoring with 30 off 20 balls and taking 2 for 10 with the ball, including the scalp of Sri Lanka's star Chamari Athapaththu. At 22, she had become the youngest captain to lead Pakistan in a T20 World Cup, taking over from veteran Nida Dar.

"When I got the captaincy I decided that I will lead from the front, so that's the main thing I did today."

— Fatima Sana, after her Player of the Match performance at the T20 World Cup

Rebuilding Under Wahab Riaz

The PCB has retained former fast bowler Wahab Riaz as head coach for both the Asia Cup and Asian Games campaigns, according to Sportstar. Riaz was appointed to the women's setup following Pakistan's dismal last-place finish at the 2025 ODI World Cup in India and Sri Lanka, where the team failed to win a single match across seven fixtures.

Under Riaz's mentorship, Sana's early captaincy has shown promise. In the series against South Africa ahead of the T20 World Cup, she topped the run charts across both teams, scoring 101 runs in three T20Is including two unbeaten thirties. The all-round performances suggested Pakistan's women's cricket was beginning to turn a corner before the personal tragedy intervened.

The India Factor

For Indian diaspora cricket fans, the Asia Cup carries particular significance. India and Pakistan's women's teams have developed an intense rivalry across recent ICC events, with their T20 World Cup encounters drawing substantial viewership globally. India's women's team, fresh off strong recent form, will be among the favourites, and any India-Pakistan clash in the Asia Cup promises to draw significant attention from South Asian communities worldwide.

The Asian Games cricket tournament adds another dimension, with medals at stake and national pride on the line. Pakistan's women have historically performed well at the Asian Games, winning gold medals in 2010 and 2014.

What's Next

Sana's return will be closely watched as a barometer of Pakistan women's cricket's trajectory. Her ability to channel personal grief into on-field performance, and whether Riaz's coaching can build on the early signs of progress, will determine whether this squad can compete seriously at both tournaments. For a team that finished last at the ODI World Cup just months ago, the stakes could not be higher.
